records.name: Mighty Writers
records.summary: A free nonprofit that helps Philadelphia kids ages 7 to 14 get better at writing. Volunteers help with homework at its after school Academy or mentor one young writer over time.
records.what_you_do: Writing Assistants help students with homework and writing, one shift of 1 to 4 hours a week. Mentors meet their mentee 2 to 4 times a month for at least a year. Big Brothers Big Sisters handles screening and matching for mentors.

schedule.text: Writing Assistant shifts of 1 to 4 hours, one a week; mentors meet 2 to 4 times a month

first_step.how: Apply through the volunteer page, and email volunteers@mightywriters.org with any questions about the background clearances
first_step.basis: Roles are listed publicly with a clear way to apply; clearances and orientation come before you start

records.notes: The volunteer page has no dated news, so status rests on a working site. Age range for Writing Assistants is not stated. Program covers Greater Philadelphia and New Jersey; no Philadelphia street address on the page. Recheck openings before publishing.

records.name: CASA of Philadelphia County
records.summary: A volunteer advocate program for children in foster care. Trained volunteers get to know one child or sibling group and report to the Family Court judge about what the child needs.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers listen to the child, talk with foster parents, parents, teachers and doctors, review records, and write recommendations for the judge. The group asks for a two year commitment and an information session first.

schedule.text: Information session first, then a two year commitment with one child or sibling group at a time

first_step.how: Register for the 30 minute information session through the link on the volunteer page
first_step.basis: You must attend an information session, pass background checks and complete training before you are matched with a child

records.notes: Not recorded from the group's page: a recruitment listing (June 2025) says volunteers must be 21 or older and give about 10 to 15 hours a month, and sources disagree on training length (30 or 32 hours). Confirm with the group. Court involvement is their core work, so court_ordered_ok was left unknown rather than inferred.

records.name: ASAP (After School Activities Partnerships)
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that runs after school clubs in chess, debate, drama and Scrabble. It works with more than 200 schools, libraries and rec centers, and invites caring adults to help kids find new interests and friends.
records.what_you_do: Adults join as volunteers to help run after school club activities. ASAP gives clubs free training and supplies. The site does not state the weekly time or what training volunteers get.

schedule.text: After school clubs meet in schools, libraries and recreation centers

cost.text: Clubs get free training and supplies

locations.label: ASAP office
locations.address: One Penn Center, 1617 John F. Kennedy Blvd, Suite 1855

records.notes: Interim executive director named on the site (no date given). A Temple listing in search results describes one club for about two hours a week for a semester; that came from a search summary, not the group's page, so it is not recorded. Clearance rules are not stated on the site; ask ASAP. Site address listed for ASAP is its office, not the club sites.

records.name: Philly Reading Coaches
records.summary: A City of Philadelphia early reading program. Volunteers sit one on one with a student in grades K to 3 during after school sessions at city out of school time programs.
records.what_you_do: Coaches read with one student for at least one hour a week. No teaching experience is needed, and the city trains volunteers. Program Aides, a supervising volunteer role, manage a team of coaches at a site, about 3 hours a week.

schedule.text: Weekly reading sessions after school; Program Aide cycle ran October 2025 to May 2026

first_step.how: Fill out the interest form from the city's program page, or email PRC@phila.gov
first_step.basis: The city says no experience is needed and trains volunteers; Program Aide listings also mention a background check and orientation

records.notes: The city's own program page at ost.phila.gov could not be opened (certificate name mismatch), so the contact email and the 2025 to 2026 cycle dates come from search summaries and the Idealist listing. No 2026 to 2027 cycle was found. The program aide listings disagree on volunteer counts. Recheck the cycle before publishing.

records.name: Minds Matter Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that prepares high achieving students from low income families for college. Volunteer mentors help two students with college planning and applications at Saturday sessions.
records.what_you_do: Mentors work with two students and a co-mentor, helping with college essays and applications. Sessions usually run Saturdays from 12:30 to 2 pm during the school year.

schedule.text: Saturday mentoring sessions, usually 12:30 to 2 pm during the school year

records.notes: The national site shows a June 2026 annual report but no Philadelphia volunteer page could be read. The Philadelphia mentor details come from a December 2025 volunteer listing on Idealist (a lead platform). Mentors need a bachelor's degree, a background check and an orientation, so newcomer friendliness is low. Recheck before publishing.

records.name: West Philadelphia Cooperative School Playgroup
records.summary: A free weekly play session for neighborhood young children and the grown-ups who bring them. It meets at the West Philadelphia Cooperative School on Baltimore Avenue.
records.what_you_do: Children play while parents or guardians stay with them. Donations are welcome but not required.

first_step.how: Email the parent member listed in the article to confirm the schedule before you go
first_step.basis: Open to all neighborhood children with a grown-up, and no one is turned away for lack of money

records.notes: The only evidence is an article dated August 2014. Confirm the playgroup still runs before showing it. The zip code is inferred from the street address, so check it.

records.name: The Philadelphia School Parent Association (TPSA)
records.summary: The parent association for The Philadelphia School. Every enrolled family belongs, and parents help with school events, the book fair, classroom reps and parent education talks.
records.what_you_do: Parents can volunteer for school events, serve as class representatives, join a committee such as the book fair, birthday table or community outreach team, or take a leadership role on the TPSA team.

first_step.how: Email tpsa@tpschool.org; enrolled families are already members
first_step.basis: Membership comes with enrollment at the school, though the page says the wider school community is welcome at committee meetings and events

records.notes: Meeting schedule is not on the page. The only dated item is a Founders Award 2026 link, which is not proof of activity. Membership is tied to attending this private school, so the open_to field is parents.

records.name: FitzPatrick Elementary Parent Volunteer Organization
records.summary: The parent volunteer group at FitzPatrick Elementary in Philadelphia. Parents help run school events and fundraisers and meet once a month during the school day.
records.what_you_do: Parent volunteers help with school events and fundraisers. Volunteers need safety clearances from the School District of Philadelphia before they work in the school.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings at the start of each month, during school hours

first_step.how: Ask any officer of the parent volunteer group, and apply through the district volunteer site
first_step.basis: Parents are welcome to volunteer, and the page names one clear route in, but clearances are required first

records.notes: The page was last modified in August 2025, which is the only date used; that is an update date, not an event date. The specific meeting day and time are not listed. The school street address is not on the page, so no location is given.

leads_only.note: Computer science tutoring and mentoring in city schools, staffed by AmeriCorps members with about 24 volunteers. The page was a search result only, not fetched.

blocked.note: Free Library tutor volunteer call returned a 403. Search summaries say kids' homework help is staff-run and teen leader roles exist; the 2023 adult tutor post is unverified.
Certificate name mismatch, so the City's Philly Reading Coaches program page could not be read. Only the phila.gov 2023 post was read.
Philadelphia chapter page not found; the root page was used instead.
Domain did not resolve. The working site (phillyasap.org) was found from a search result and read.

notes: Ran 9 of 10 WebSearch calls and about 24 WebFetch calls. The lane is narrow in Philadelphia; many tutoring and parent group sites are either undated, unreachable or only in search summaries, so I wrote 8 records and held the rest as leads or blocked rather than guess. Several records (Minds Matter, Philly Reading Coaches, West Philadelphia playgroup) rest partly on lead platforms or old articles and are marked low or medium confidence. The West Philadelphia playgroup evidence is from 2014 and is marked dormant. One search remains unused. No record uses court_ordered_ok or service_hours_letter as yes, and none of the CASA court role was inferred as court ordered.
